title: One contract number, paid in all eight years
question: Which single contracts were paid in every fiscal year from 2019 to 2026, so that the work was never put out again in that time?
finding: Of 24,301 contract numbers in the payment file, 232 were paid in every one of the eight years, $9.37 billion between them; 119 of them have a term of ten years or more in the contract table. 152 are keyed as competed and 18 under a rule that sets competition aside ($170.0 million). The largest of those 18: Epic State and Local Government LLC (Public Health, $124.4 million, sole source, term 2018–2027); Carahsoft Technology Corp (Assessor - Recorder, $8.7 million, sole source, term 2018–2030); Tides Center (Homelessness Services, $7.4 million, sole source, term 2018–2026); 21 Tech (Treasurer-Tax Collector, $6.7 million, sole source, term 2013–2033).
how: Each payment line carries a contract number. A contract is listed when payments under its number were issued in every fiscal year 2019 to 2026 (the year is read from each voucher number, not from the year the file lists the line under); a new competition would have produced a new number. Term dates and the agreed amount come from the Supplier Contracts table, the rule from the payment lines. Contracts under a rule that sets competition aside come first, then by amount paid. Payments to public bodies are left out.
limits: A contract paid for eight years may have been written for ten: construction programmes, software licences, leases and long service contracts can run that long, and most of those listed are keyed as competed. The table shows today’s end date, not the original one, so it cannot say by itself how often a contract was extended; the amended-again screen shows that for agreements large enough to need a Board vote. What would settle a row: the original term and options in the contract, and the sole-source justification where the rule sets competition aside. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. The $992.6 million of outside spending that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier is in none of the figures here; it is used only to tell that a payee is not new.
